- **Additional PIPJ procedures** for residual contracture: **check-rein ligament release, volar plate release, accessory collateral ligament release**; **beware of central slip attenuation (residual extension lag)**.
- **Salvage:** **PIPJ arthrodesis**, **amputation** (multiple recurrences, severe little finger contractures), **dynamic external fixation (Digit Widget/TEC: continuous elongation: severe PIPJ contractures)**.
- **Post-operative: night extension splint (common, evidence of benefit limited)**, hand therapy.
### Comparisons
- **Recurrence: dermofasciectomy < limited fasciectomy < collagenase ≈ needle fasciotomy.**
- **Recovery and complications: needle/collagenase faster but higher recurrence**; **surgery more durable but longer recovery**. **DISC trial (UK)**: collagenase vs limited fasciectomy: **surgery slightly better** clinically.

## 7. Complications of surgery
- **Digital nerve injury (about 2-3% primary; up to about 10% in revision)** (spiral cord), **digital artery injury (devascularisation: white finger after release: release tension (flex the finger), warm, topical vasodilators; microvascular repair)**, **haematoma**, **skin necrosis (flap tips)**, **infection**, **"flare reaction" (pain, swelling, stiffness: pseudo-CRPS: women)**, **CRPS (about 5%)**, **recurrence (true recurrence in the operated field) vs extension (new disease outside the field)**, **loss of flexion**, **PIPJ extension lag**.

# Part B: Rheumatoid hand and wrist

## 8. General principles
- **Chronic symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis**; **synovitis**: **pannus (proliferating synovium)** erodes cartilage, bone, **ligaments and tendons**; **tendon rupture by attrition or direct infiltration**.
- **Modern DMARDs/biologics** have **reduced the need for surgery**; **surgery: relieve pain, prevent tendon rupture (synovectomy), restore function, correct deformity**.
- **Priority of surgery (general principles):** **lower limb before upper limb**, **proximal before distal** (shoulder/elbow before wrist/hand), **wrist before fingers (stable wrist = foundation)**, **painful procedures first**; **joints before tendons** (or tendon transfers after joint stabilisation); **prophylactic tenosynovectomy** to prevent rupture (**over 4-6 months of persistent tenosynovitis despite medical therapy**).
- **Cervical spine assessment (atlantoaxial instability) before anaesthesia (flexion-extension radiographs)**; **perioperative DMARD management (methotrexate continued; biologics withheld around surgery)**.

## 9. Wrist
- **Caput ulnae syndrome**: **dorsal subluxation of the ulnar head** (**DRUJ synovitis with destruction of the TFCC and ECU subsheath; ECU subluxates volarly**: becomes a wrist flexor), **supination of the carpus** off the ulna, **radial deviation of the wrist** (**contributes to ulnar deviation of the fingers: "zig-zag deformity"**), **"piano key sign"** (ulnar head ballottement).
- **Carpal supination, volar subluxation, ulnar translocation of the carpus** (radiocarpal ligament destruction).
- **Vaughan-Jackson syndrome** (**attrition rupture of the ulnar extensors (EDM first, then EDC little and ring) over the prominent dorsal ulnar head**).
- **Mannerfelt-Norman syndrome** (**attrition rupture of the FPL** (then FDP index) **over a scaphoid/STT osteophyte** in the carpal tunnel).
- **Differentials of loss of finger extension in RA:**
  1. **Extensor tendon rupture** (**tenodesis test: passive wrist flexion fails to extend the MCPJs**),
  2. **PIN palsy** (**elbow synovitis compressing the PIN**; **tenodesis effect intact**),
  3. **Extensor tendon subluxation into the ulnar gutter at the MCPJ** (**sagittal band attenuation: patient can maintain extension once passively extended**),
  4. **MCPJ volar dislocation/subluxation** (cannot be passively extended).
- **Surgical options:**
  - **Dorsal tenosynovectomy + extensor retinaculum transposed beneath the tendons** (protects them).
  - **Distal ulna procedures:** **Darrach (distal ulna excision)** (**low-demand elderly; risk of ulnar stump instability/convergence**), **Sauvé-Kapandji (DRUJ arthrodesis + proximal ulnar pseudarthrosis)** (**younger; preserves ulnar support for the carpus: prevents ulnar translocation**), **ulnar head replacement**.
  - **Tendon transfer/reconstruction for ruptures:** **single EDC rupture: side-to-side transfer to adjacent EDC**; **two tendons (little and ring): side-to-side + EIP transfer**; **three or more: FDS transfer (ring/middle) or free grafts**; **EPL rupture: EIP to EPL**; **FPL rupture: FDS ring transfer or IPJ fusion**.
  - **Radiolunate (Chamay) fusion** (**prevents ulnar translocation; partial fusion when the midcarpal joint is preserved**).
  - **Total wrist arthrodesis** (**gold standard for the destroyed rheumatoid wrist**; **Mannerfelt pin, Steinmann pin or plate**; **fuse in neutral or slight extension; if bilateral, consider one arthroplasty or fuse one in slight flexion for perineal hygiene**).
  - **Total wrist arthroplasty**: **low-demand, bilateral disease, good bone stock**; preserves motion; higher complication rates.
  - **Larsen grading** of radiological destruction (0-5).

## 10. MCP joints
- **Ulnar drift and volar subluxation** (**the commonest finger deformity in RA**):
  - **Synovitis stretches the radial sagittal band and collateral ligaments**,
  - **Extensor tendons sublux ulnarly into the valleys between the metacarpal heads**,
  - **Radial deviation of the wrist (with metacarpals) + ulnar pull of flexor tendons (enter the finger obliquely) + intrinsic contracture (ulnar intrinsics)** + **gravity/pinch forces** (**thumb pushes the index ulnarly**),
  - **Volar plate and accessory collateral ligament destruction**: **volar subluxation of the proximal phalanx**.
- **Treatment:**
  - **Early (no joint destruction): synovectomy, extensor tendon centralisation (sagittal band reefing), intrinsic release (cross-intrinsic transfer: ulnar intrinsic of one finger to the radial lateral band of the adjacent finger)**.
  - **Joint destruction: silicone MCPJ arthroplasty (Swanson: a flexible spacer; encapsulation)** with **soft-tissue rebalancing (radial collateral ligament reconstruction, centralisation, intrinsic release)**: **pain relief, improved arc and appearance (arc about 40-60 degrees, shifted into extension)**; **implant fracture (about 10-30% at 10 years), silicone synovitis (rare at the MCPJ), recurrent ulnar drift**. **Correct wrist radial deviation first** (otherwise recurrence).
  - **Pyrocarbon/surface replacement**: requires intact soft tissues (less used in RA).

## 11. Finger deformities
### Swan-neck deformity (PIPJ hyperextension + DIPJ flexion)
- **Origins:** **MCPJ (volar subluxation/intrinsic tightness: commonest in RA)**, **PIPJ (volar plate laxity, synovitis, FDS rupture)**, **DIPJ (mallet: terminal tendon rupture)**.
- **Nalebuff classification (RA swan-neck):**
  - **Type I: PIPJ flexible in all MCPJ positions**: **splint (figure-of-eight/ring splint)**, **DIPJ fusion (mallet)**, **dermodesis, flexor tenodesis (FDS sling), SORL (spiral oblique retinacular ligament reconstruction)**,
  - **Type II: PIPJ flexion limited with the MCPJ extended (intrinsic tightness: positive Bunnell-Littler/Finochietto test)**: **intrinsic release** + type I procedures,
  - **Type III: PIPJ stiff in all positions, joint surface preserved**: **PIPJ manipulation, lateral band mobilisation, skin release (dorsal)**, **flexor tenosynovectomy**,
  - **Type IV: PIPJ stiff with joint destruction**: **PIPJ arthrodesis (index/middle: lateral pinch stability) or arthroplasty (ring/little)**.
### Boutonniere deformity (PIPJ flexion + DIPJ hyperextension)
- **PIPJ synovitis**: **central slip attenuation**, **lateral bands migrate volarly** (triangular ligament stretched).
- **Nalebuff/Millender stages:**
  - **Stage I (mild: 10-15 degree PIPJ extension lag, passively correctable)**: **splinting**, **synovectomy**, **Fowler/Dolphin terminal tendon tenotomy** (DIPJ hyperextension),
  - **Stage II (moderate: about 30-40 degree lag, passively correctable)**: **central slip reconstruction (Matev/Curtis), lateral band relocation**,
  - **Stage III (fixed, joint destroyed)**: **PIPJ arthrodesis (index/middle) or arthroplasty**.
### Thumb deformities (Nalebuff classification: types I-VI)
- **Type I: boutonniere thumb (commonest: about 50-70%)**: **MCPJ flexion + IPJ hyperextension** (**MCPJ synovitis stretches the EPB insertion and dorsal capsule; EPL subluxes ulnarly/volarly**): **early: synovectomy + EPL rerouting (to the dorsal base of the proximal phalanx)**; **late: MCPJ arthrodesis (± IPJ arthrodesis/arthroplasty)**.
- **Type II: rare (boutonniere + CMCJ subluxation)**.
- **Type III: swan-neck thumb (second commonest)**: **CMCJ subluxation/adduction contracture**: **MCPJ hyperextension + IPJ flexion** (like OA): **CMCJ arthroplasty (trapeziectomy) + MCPJ fusion/volar capsulodesis**, **first web release**.
- **Type IV: gamekeeper's (UCL laxity: MCPJ radial deviation, secondary adduction)**: **UCL reconstruction or MCPJ arthrodesis**.
- **Type V: MCPJ volar plate laxity (MCPJ hyperextension, IPJ flexion; CMCJ normal)**: **volar capsulodesis/MCPJ fusion**.
- **Type VI: arthritis mutilans (opera-glass hand)**: **bone resorption, shortening, "telescoping"**: **arthrodesis with bone grafting** to restore length.

## 12. Other inflammatory hand conditions
- **Psoriatic arthritis:** **DIPJ involvement**, **pencil-in-cup deformity**, **arthritis mutilans**, **dactylitis (sausage digit)**, **nail pitting**, **asymmetric**; **stiffness (ankylosis) rather than instability**; **avoid surgery through active psoriatic plaques (infection risk)**; **arthrodesis in functional position** commonly.
- **Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE):** **ligamentous laxity with reducible deformities (Jaccoud arthropathy: ulnar drift, swan neck) WITHOUT joint destruction**: **soft-tissue procedures fail (recurrence): arthrodesis often preferred**.
- **Scleroderma (systemic sclerosis):** **PIPJ flexion contractures** (**dorsal skin ulceration over the PIPJ**), **Raynaud phenomenon, digital ischaemic ulcers**, **calcinosis (CREST)**, **acro-osteolysis**; **PIPJ arthrodesis (with shortening)**, **digital sympathectomy (periarterial)**, **botulinum toxin for Raynaud**, **calcinosis excision**.
- **Gout:** **tophi (urate deposits)**, **flexor tenosynovitis, carpal tunnel syndrome**, **punched-out erosions with overhanging edges ("rat bite")**; **debulking of tophi** for skin ulceration, infection, nerve compression.
- **Osteoarthritis of the hand (comparison):** **Heberden nodes (DIPJ)**, **Bouchard nodes (PIPJ)**, **thumb CMCJ (basal joint) OA (Eaton-Littler stages I-IV: trapeziectomy ± LRTI for stages II-IV; CMCJ arthrodesis in young manual workers)**, **mucous cyst (DIPJ OA ganglion: excise with osteophyte)**.

> Exam pearl: **Dupuytren: myofibroblast, type III collagen up, TGF-beta. Diathesis: early onset, family history, bilateral, ectopic (Garrod, Ledderhose, Peyronie). Cleland ligament spared; Grayson involved. Spiral cord (pretendinous band + spiral band + lateral digital sheet + Grayson) displaces the NV bundle central, superficial, proximal.**

> Exam pearl: **Operate for MCPJ over 30 degrees, any PIPJ contracture, positive tabletop test. Recurrence: dermofasciectomy lowest; needle and collagenase highest. Collagenase: skin tears; tendon rupture rare. White finger after release: flex finger, warm.**

> Exam pearl: **RA: caput ulnae (dorsal ulnar head, ECU volar), Vaughan-Jackson (EDM first), Mannerfelt (FPL over scaphoid). Loss of finger extension: rupture (tenodesis test negative), PIN palsy (tenodesis intact), subluxed tendon (holds once placed), MCPJ dislocation. Darrach (elderly) vs Sauvé-Kapandji (young). Wrist fusion is gold standard; correct wrist radial deviation before MCPJ silicone arthroplasty.**

> Exam pearl: **Swan-neck Nalebuff I flexible, II intrinsic tight, III stiff/joint preserved, IV destroyed. Boutonniere thumb (type I) commonest RA thumb deformity. SLE: reducible deformities without destruction (Jaccoud); soft-tissue procedures fail. Psoriatic: DIPJ, pencil-in-cup. Scleroderma: PIPJ flexion, calcinosis.**

congenital hand.md:
## 1. Embryology
- **Upper limb bud appears at about day 26-28 of gestation**; **limb development is complete by about week 8** (most congenital differences arise between **weeks 4 and 8**).
- **Signalling centres (three axes):**
| Axis | Signalling centre | Molecule | Defects |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Proximal-distal** | **Apical ectodermal ridge (AER)** | **Fibroblast growth factors (FGF-4, FGF-8)** | **Transverse deficiencies (amputations)**, **symbrachydactyly** |
| **Anterior-posterior (radial-ulnar)** | **Zone of polarising activity (ZPA)** (posterior mesoderm) | **Sonic hedgehog (SHH)** | **Mirror hand (ulnar dimelia: SHH duplication)**, **polydactyly**, **radial/ulnar deficiencies** |
| **Dorsal-ventral** | **Dorsal ectoderm** (**Wnt-7a**) / ventral ectoderm (**engrailed-1 (EN-1)** suppresses Wnt-7a) | **Wnt-7a**, **LMX1B** (dorsal mesoderm) | **Nail-patella syndrome (LMX1B: absent/hypoplastic nails, absent patella)**, **dorsal dimelia (palmar nails)** |
- **Digit separation:** **apoptosis** of interdigital tissue (**bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs)**) at about **weeks 6-8**: failure = **syndactyly**.
- **HOX genes** (HOXA13, HOXD13: **synpolydactyly**).

## 2. Classification
- **Swanson (IFSSH, 1976) classification (historical, 7 groups):**
  1. **Failure of formation** (transverse: congenital amputations; longitudinal: radial/ulnar/central deficiencies),
  2. **Failure of differentiation (separation)** (syndactyly, camptodactyly, clinodactyly, arthrogryposis, synostosis),
  3. **Duplication** (polydactyly, mirror hand),
  4. **Overgrowth** (macrodactyly),
  5. **Undergrowth** (thumb hypoplasia, brachydactyly),
  6. **Constriction band syndrome**,
  7. **Generalised skeletal abnormalities**.
- **OMT classification (Oberg-Manske-Tonkin; adopted by IFSSH 2014)**: **Malformations** (abnormal axis formation/differentiation: **proximal-distal, radial-ulnar, dorsal-ventral, unspecified axis**), **Deformations** (constriction ring), **Dysplasias** (hypertrophy: macrodactyly; tumorous conditions), **Syndromes**.

## 3. Syndactyly
- **Commonest congenital hand anomaly (about 1 in 2,000-2,500 live births)**; **boys 2:1**; **bilateral about 50%**; **familial (autosomal dominant with variable penetrance) in about 10-40%**.
- **Commonest site: third web space (middle-ring fingers) (about 50%)**, then 4th, 2nd, 1st (rare).
- **Classification:**
  - **Simple** (skin/soft tissue only) vs **complex** (**bony fusion: side-to-side, usually distal phalanges**),
  - **Complete** (extends to the fingertip) vs **incomplete**,
  - **Complicated** (**abnormal bones: e.g. Apert syndrome, synpolydactyly**).
- **Associated syndromes:**
  - **Apert syndrome (acrocephalosyndactyly; FGFR2 mutation)**: **craniosynostosis, mid-face hypoplasia, complex "mitten hand" syndactyly (rosebud hand)**, **symphalangism**, **radial clinodactyly of the thumb (delta phalanx)**,
  - **Poland syndrome**: **unilateral absence of the sternocostal head of pectoralis major**, **ipsilateral symbrachydactyly (short webbed fingers: hypoplastic middle phalanges)**, **breast/nipple hypoplasia**,
  - **Constriction band syndrome (acrosyndactyly: fenestrated distal fusion with proximal sinus tracts)**,
  - **Carpenter syndrome**, **Pfeiffer syndrome**.
- **Timing of release:**
  - **Border digits (thumb-index, ring-little) first and earlier (about 6-12 months)**: **unequal lengths cause progressive tethering/angular deformity of the longer digit**,
  - **Central digits (middle-ring): about 12-18 months** (before school age),
  - **Release only one side of a digit at a time** (**never both sides of a finger simultaneously: risk of vascular compromise**),
  - Complex syndactyly: earlier staged release.
- **Technique:** **dorsal rectangular or pentagonal flap to reconstruct the web commissure** (**the commissure slopes from dorsal-proximal to palmar-distal at about 45 degrees**), **interdigitating zig-zag flaps**, **full-thickness skin grafts (groin/antecubital)** for skin deficit (**syndactylised digits share skin: almost always need grafts**); **Buck-Gramcko pulp plasty** for fingertip separation (nail folds).
- **Complications:** **web creep (commonest: distal migration of the web: especially with split-thickness grafts or early surgery)**, **flexion contractures (scar)**, **graft loss**, **nail deformity**, **vascular compromise**, **angular deformity**.

## 4. Polydactyly
- **Postaxial (ulnar) polydactyly:** **commonest overall** (**about 10x more common in individuals of African descent**; **autosomal dominant**); **Temtamy and McKusick: type A (well-formed digit articulating with the fifth/sixth metacarpal)**, **type B (rudimentary, pedunculated skin tag ("nubbin"))**. **In Caucasians, postaxial polydactyly suggests a syndrome** (e.g. **Ellis-van Creveld (chondroectodermal dysplasia)**, **Bardet-Biedl**, **trisomy 13**): **genetic evaluation**. **Type B: suture ligation in the nursery (risk of a residual bump/neuroma) or surgical excision**; **type A: surgical excision with reconstruction of the collateral ligament/hypothenar muscle (ADM) insertion** at about **9-12 months**.
- **Preaxial (radial) polydactyly = thumb duplication:**
  - **Commonest in Asians and Caucasians among radial anomalies**; **usually sporadic, unilateral**.
  - **Wassel classification (level of duplication; odd numbers = bifid (partial), even numbers = complete duplication):**
    - **I** bifid distal phalanx,
    - **II** duplicated distal phalanx,
    - **III** bifid proximal phalanx,
    - **IV** **duplicated proximal phalanx (commonest: about 45%)**,
    - **V** bifid metacarpal,
    - **VI** duplicated metacarpal,
    - **VII** **triphalangeal thumb component** (associated with **Holt-Oram syndrome, Fanconi anaemia (VII + radial deficiency)**, autosomal dominant triphalangeal thumb).
  - **Wassel-Flatt** (modified) and **Rotterdam classification** (more inclusive).
  - **Treatment (about 12 months): excise the hypoplastic (usually radial) thumb**, **preserve and reconstruct the radial collateral ligament** (**reattach to the retained thumb with a periosteal sleeve**), **reattach the thenar muscles (APB) to the retained thumb**, **correct the axis (osteotomy)** and **centralise the tendons (FPL/EPL eccentric insertions)**; **Bilhaut-Cloquet procedure** (**central wedge resection and combination of both halves**: equal-sized hypoplastic thumbs: Wassel I/II; risk of **nail deformity and physeal mismatch/stiffness**).
  - **Complications:** **Z-deformity (zigzag: angular deformity at the IPJ/MCPJ)** (commonest late problem: from unbalanced tendons/collateral ligaments), **instability**, **stiffness**, residual nail deformity.
- **Central polydactyly** (index, middle, ring duplications): often with **syndactyly (synpolydactyly: HOXD13)**; complex reconstruction.
- **Mirror hand (ulnar dimelia)**: **duplication of ulnar side (two ulnae, no radius, multiple fingers (7-8), no thumb)**: **ZPA duplication (SHH)**; **pollicisation of one digit + excision**.

## 5. Radial longitudinal deficiency (radial club hand)
- **Spectrum** of hypoplasia of the radius and pre-axial (thumb) structures: **about 1 in 30,000-100,000**; **bilateral about 50%**; **thumb always involved** (hypoplasia/absence).
- **Bayne and Klug classification (radius):**
  - **Type 0:** **normal radius length** (carpal deficiency/thumb hypoplasia only) (added later),
  - **Type I:** **short distal radius** (delayed distal radial physis),
  - **Type II:** **hypoplastic radius** (miniature, both physes),
  - **Type III:** **partial absence** (usually distal: commonest),
  - **Type IV:** **complete absence of the radius (commonest overall: about 50%)**.
  - (**James/Manske modified: type N** (thumb only), **type 0** (carpal anomalies with normal radius length)).
- **Associated syndromes (screen all patients):**
  - **VACTERL** (Vertebral, Anal atresia, Cardiac, TracheoEsophageal fistula, Renal, Limb anomalies),
  - **Holt-Oram syndrome** (**cardiac septal defects: ASD/VSD; TBX5, autosomal dominant**),
  - **TAR syndrome** (**thrombocytopenia-absent radius**: **thumbs PRESENT** (unique); platelets improve after the first year; autosomal recessive (RBM8A)),
  - **Fanconi anaemia** (**aplastic anaemia (develops about age 6-7: chromosomal breakage test: DEB/mitomycin C)**; needs **bone marrow transplant**; screening is essential),
  - **Trisomy 13/18**.
  - **Investigations: CBC/platelets, echocardiogram, renal ultrasound, spine radiographs, chromosomal breakage test (Fanconi)**.
- **Clinical:** **radially deviated, short forearm**, **ulna bowed (towards the radius)**, **thumb hypoplasia/absence**, **stiff elbow (elbow extension contracture: contraindicates centralisation, as the radially deviated wrist allows the hand to reach the mouth)**; **radial nerve absence distal to the elbow (superficial radial nerve replaced by the median nerve)**; **radial artery absent**.
- **Treatment:**
  - **Early: stretching and splinting** (from birth).
  - **Types I-II (mild)**: stretching/splinting; **radial lengthening**.
  - **Types III-IV**: **centralisation (placing the carpus on the distal ulna)** or **radialisation (Buck-Gramcko: carpus over-corrected onto the ulna with transfer of radial wrist extensors to the ulnar side)** at **about 6-12 months** (after soft-tissue distraction with an external fixator), followed by **pollicisation (of the index finger) for an absent/non-reconstructable thumb**; **ulnar osteotomy** for bowing.
  - **Contraindications to centralisation:** **stiff elbow (extension contracture: patient needs radial deviation to reach the mouth)**, **adults who have adapted well**, **severe associated medical conditions (short life expectancy)**.
  - **Recurrence of radial deviation (commonest complication)**, **ulnar physeal damage (growth arrest)**, stiffness.

## 6. Thumb hypoplasia
- **Blauth classification (modified by Manske):**
  - **Type I:** **minor generalised hypoplasia** (all elements present, small): no treatment,
  - **Type II:** **thenar muscle hypoplasia, first web space narrowing, ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) instability of the MCPJ**: **opponensplasty (Huber: ADM transfer; or FDS ring)**, **first web deepening (4-flap Z-plasty)**, **UCL reconstruction**,
  - **Type III:** **extrinsic tendon abnormalities (pollex abductus: FPL connection to EPL)**, **hypoplastic metacarpal**: **IIIA: stable CMCJ (basal joint present)**: **reconstruct (like type II + extrinsic tendon correction)**; **IIIB: unstable CMCJ (absent base of metacarpal)**: **pollicisation** (Manske: **critical distinction: presence of a stable CMCJ**),
  - **Type IV:** **pouce flottant ("floating thumb"): rudimentary thumb attached by a skin bridge**: **pollicisation**,
  - **Type V:** **absent thumb**: **pollicisation**.
- **Pollicisation (Buck-Gramcko technique)**: **index finger transferred to the thumb position**: **rotated about 120-160 degrees (pronation)**, **abducted about 40 degrees**, **shortened** (**index MCPJ becomes the new CMCJ; metacarpal head becomes the trapezium; PIPJ becomes the MCPJ**); **first dorsal interosseous becomes APB/abductor**, **first palmar interosseous becomes adductor**, **EIP becomes EPL**, **EDC (index) becomes APL**; **at about 12-18 months**.

## 7. Ulnar longitudinal deficiency
- **Less common than radial (about 1:4-10 relative frequency)**; **not associated with systemic syndromes** (unlike radial deficiency) but **associated with other musculoskeletal anomalies (PFFD, fibular hemimelia, scoliosis)** and **hand anomalies (ulnar digits absent, syndactyly)**.
- **Bayne classification:** **I hypoplastic ulna**, **II partial aplasia**, **III total aplasia**, **IV radiohumeral synostosis**.
- **Elbow instability or synostosis** (vs radial deficiency: wrist is relatively stable).
- **Treatment:** focus on **hand function (syndactyly release, thumb reconstruction, first web)**; **excision of the ulnar anlage** (fibrocartilaginous band that tethers the radius: progressive bowing/radial head dislocation), **one-bone forearm** for severe instability.

## 8. Central deficiency (cleft hand) vs symbrachydactyly
| Feature | **Cleft hand (typical; central longitudinal deficiency)** | **Symbrachydactyly (atypical cleft)** |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | **V-shaped central cleft** (missing middle ray) | **U-shaped**; **short digits with nubbins (rudimentary nails)** |
| Inheritance | **Autosomal dominant; often bilateral**; **feet involved (split hand-foot malformation: SHFM)** | **Sporadic, unilateral** |
| Associations | **EEC syndrome (ectrodactyly-ectodermal dysplasia-clefting)**, syndactyly of the first web | **Poland syndrome** |
| Mechanism | **AER (central) failure** | **AER/mesoderm (proximal-distal) failure: transverse spectrum** |
| Function | **Often excellent ("functional triumph, aesthetic disaster" (Flatt))** | Variable |
| Treatment | **Cleft closure (Snow-Littler, Ueba, Miura)** + **first web release** (**syndactyly of the first web: release first**); **transposition of the index ray** to the third metacarpal position | **Non-vascularised toe phalanx transfer** (**under 18 months: physis survives**), **free toe transfer**, **distraction lengthening**, **web deepening** |

## 9. Camptodactyly and clinodactyly
### Camptodactyly
- **Non-traumatic flexion contracture of the PIPJ** (**little finger commonest**; **bilateral about 2/3**); **infantile (equal sexes)** and **adolescent (girls; progressive during growth spurt)** forms.
- **Cause:** **abnormal lumbrical insertion (commonest)**, **FDS contracture/abnormal origin**, **skin deficiency**, volar plate contracture, **abnormal insertion of the lumbrical/interosseous into the FDS or capsule**.
- **Radiographs (late):** **flattening (notching) of the neck of the proximal phalanx, flattened/indented base of the middle phalanx, volar subluxation**.
- **Treatment:** **splinting and stretching (mainstay; most effective under about 3 years and in flexible deformity)**; **surgery (FDS tenotomy/lengthening, abnormal lumbrical release, volar plate release, skin flaps/grafts)** for **contractures over 30-60 degrees with functional impairment or progression despite splinting**; **outcomes are unpredictable** (stiffness, loss of flexion).
### Clinodactyly
- **Angular deformity in the radioulnar (coronal) plane**, **little finger (radial deviation at the DIPJ) commonest**; **middle phalanx**: **trapezoidal or triangular (delta phalanx: longitudinal epiphyseal bracket (C-shaped physis))**.
- **Associations:** **Down syndrome (about 35-80%)**, Klinefelter, Turner, **Rubinstein-Taybi (broad thumbs, delta phalanx)**, **Apert**.
- **Treatment:** **observation (most: cosmetic)**; **surgery if over 30 degrees with functional impairment/overlapping**: **opening-wedge, closing-wedge or reverse-wedge osteotomy**; **physiolysis (Vickers: excision of the longitudinal bracket with fat interposition)** in **young children (under 6 years: allows growth to correct)**.
- **Kirner deformity**: **palmar-radial curvature of the distal phalanx of the little finger** (**girls 8-14 years**): observation/osteotomy.

## 10. Other conditions
- **Trigger thumb (paediatric):** **not truly congenital (develops after birth; usually noticed at 1-3 years)**; **fixed flexion of the IPJ** with a **Notta node (nodule in the FPL at the A1 pulley)**; **about 30% resolve spontaneously (more under 1 year)**; **A1 pulley release** if persistent beyond about **3 years** (or earlier if fixed) (**the radial digital nerve is close and superficial: at risk**).
- **Trigger finger (paediatric):** rarer; **anatomical abnormalities (FDS decussation, abnormal slips, nodules)**: **A1 release alone is often insufficient: excise one slip of FDS ± A3 release**.
- **Congenital clasped thumb:** **absent/hypoplastic EPB/EPL** (thumb flexed across the palm); **splinting (3-6 months)**; **tendon transfer (EIP to EPL)** and **web reconstruction** if it fails; associated with **arthrogryposis** (**complex clasped thumb**).
- **Constriction ring (amniotic band) syndrome:** **circumferential constriction rings**, **acrosyndactyly (fenestrated distal syndactyly)**, **amputations**, **lymphoedema distal to the ring**; **not genetic (sporadic)**; **urgent release for vascular compromise (neonatal emergency)**; **staged Z-plasty/W-plasty release (half the circumference at a time traditionally; single-stage now common)**.
- **Macrodactyly:** **true overgrowth of all tissues of a digit** (**PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS)**; **lipofibromatous hamartoma of the median nerve** ("nerve territory-oriented macrodactyly": index/middle)); **static vs progressive**; **epiphysiodesis, debulking, ray amputation**; differentials: **Proteus syndrome**, **neurofibromatosis**, **Klippel-Trenaunay**, **Ollier/Maffucci**.
- **Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (amyoplasia commonest)**: **internally rotated shoulders, extended elbows, flexed and ulnarly deviated wrists, thumb-in-palm**, **symmetrical limb involvement, absent skin creases**, **normal intelligence and sensation**; **early stretching/serial casting**; **elbow flexion (passive flexion first: posterior capsulotomy + triceps lengthening; then tendon transfers (triceps to biceps, pectoralis, latissimus))**; **wrist: dorsal closing-wedge carpal osteotomy**.
- **Congenital radioulnar synostosis:** **proximal (commonest)**, **fixed pronation**, **often bilateral**; **AD inheritance in some; associated with sex chromosome anomalies (XXY)**; **no rotation (no supination)**; **observation if pronation under about 60 degrees** (**compensated by shoulder/wrist**); **derotational osteotomy through the synostosis to about 10-20 degrees pronation (dominant) and neutral/slight supination (non-dominant)** if severe (over about 60 degrees); **compartment syndrome and vascular compromise risk with large rotations**; **resection of the synostosis fails (re-forms)**.
- **Madelung deformity:** **volar-ulnar tethering of the distal radial physis (Vickers ligament: abnormal radiolunate ligament)**: **volar and ulnar tilt of the distal radius, dorsally prominent ulna**, **adolescent girls, bilateral**; **Léri-Weill dyschondrosteosis (SHOX gene)**; **Vickers ligament release with physiolysis (younger)**, **dome osteotomy of the radius ± ulnar shortening** (older).
- **Congenital radial head dislocation:** **usually posterior**, bilateral, **convex radial head, hypoplastic capitellum** (vs traumatic: concave head, normal capitellum); **associated with syndromes (nail-patella, Ehlers-Danlos)**; **observe; excise the radial head at maturity** if painful.

> Exam pearl: **AER (FGF) = proximal-distal (transverse deficiency); ZPA (SHH) = radial-ulnar (polydactyly, mirror hand); Wnt-7a/LMX1B = dorsal-ventral (nail-patella). OMT classification replaced Swanson.**

> Exam pearl: **Syndactyly: commonest; 3rd web; border digits first (6-12 months); never both sides of one digit; dorsal flap commissure + FTSG; web creep. Apert (FGFR2) = complex mitten hand; Poland = pectoralis head + symbrachydactyly.**

> Exam pearl: **Thumb duplication: Wassel IV commonest; excise radial thumb, keep RCL and thenar insertion; Bilhaut-Cloquet for equal halves; Z-deformity late. Postaxial polydactyly in Caucasians = syndrome (Ellis-van Creveld).**

> Exam pearl: **Radial deficiency: screen for VACTERL, Holt-Oram (heart), TAR (thumbs present), Fanconi (chromosomal breakage). Bayne IV commonest. Centralisation/radialisation contraindicated with a stiff elbow. Blauth IIIA reconstruct, IIIB/IV/V pollicise (stable CMCJ is the key). Pollicisation: index rotated about 120-160 degrees; MCPJ becomes CMCJ.**

> Exam pearl: **Cleft hand (V, bilateral, feet, AD) vs symbrachydactyly (U, unilateral, nubbins, Poland). Camptodactyly: PIPJ little finger (lumbrical), splint. Clinodactyly: delta phalanx, physiolysis under 6. Paediatric trigger thumb: Notta node, release after 3 years (radial digital nerve at risk). Synostosis: osteotomy, not resection. Madelung: Vickers ligament, SHOX.**
